newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Strong buying interest lifts Mauritius mart index.
newsitem.headline: Strong buying interest lifts Mauritius mart index.

text.p: The Mauritius bourse index Semdex rose on Friday, fuelled by upward moving stocks that were led by shares in the banking sector, brokers said.
The Semdex rose 2.44 points to 333.28 with turnover unofficially posted at 12.71 million rupees on 923,277 shares from 29.76 million rupees on 2,105,709 shares on Wednesday.
Moving stocks were mostly up and strong buying interest was seen on those in the banking sector, brokers said.
"Foreign investors again bought State Bank of Mauritius just like during the last trading session on Wednesday," one senior broker said.

"Together with the other banking stock (Mauritius Commercial Bank), these two shares are leading the Semdex up owing to their high weight in the index. By extension, investors are encouraged to buy elsewhere in the market," the broker added.
State Bank of Mauritius rose 10 cents to another all time high of 9.30 rupees on 582,000 shares and Mauritius Commercial Bank gained 50 cents to 74 rupees on 18,150 shares.
Market observers did not exclude the possibility of a recovery in the Mauritian stock market which was depressed during the last six months on political uncertainty.

"I am prudently bullish. The economy and (company) fundamentals are going well and the market is waiting for an increase in capital flow next year," said Thierry Hugnin of General Brokerage, referring to a second country fund which is expected to invest 300 million rupees ($15 million) in the Mauritius bourse in early 1997.

"Unfortunately, there is still the risk of socio-political factors overshadowing the fundamentals as they did this year. But we think that the market will now be able to concentrate on the fundamentals," Hugnin added.
In the rest of the trading session, commerce based Happy World Foods attracted another big deal. It gained 20 cents to 17.20 rupees on a heavy 175,000 shares.
British American Insurance was unchanged at 7.50 rupees on 21,350 shares. Construction materials manufacturer United Basalt Products was 1.10 rupees higher to 30.50 on 1,100 shares.
